top.headline: Trump's Ambassador to Greece Resigns Amid Misconduct Allegations
top.blurb: Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned as US ambassador to Greece after the White House asked her to step down, following allegations first reported by the Wall Street Journal that she asked a Trump donor to cover a $100,000 personal credit card bill in exchange for access to administration officials. She has called the claims false and says she intends to contest them.

top.headline: Taxpayer-Funded Pro-Trump Ads Kept Airing After a Judge Ordered Them Pulled
top.blurb: A federal judge issued a restraining order barring further taxpayer funding for TV ads boosting Republicans ahead of the midterms, but an NPR analysis found nearly $22 million had already been spent since late September. The White House says it has no immediate plans to repay the roughly $20 million in public funds used.

top.headline: Delhi Police Beat and Detain a Caravan Journalist Covering CEC Protests
top.blurb: Delhi Police dragged Caravan multimedia producer Ryan Thomas into a detention bus and struck him when he refused to delete footage of a protest detention, despite his press card being visibly displayed, the magazine reported. The Committee to Protect Journalists counted at least 37 journalists detained over two days covering protests against Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, defying a Supreme Court directive issued the same week that police not hinder press coverage.

top.headline: Houthis Strike Saudi Aramco Facility as Saudi Coalition Hits Oil Sites in Sanaa
top.blurb: Houthi forces targeted an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran hours after the Saudi-led coalition struck an oil site in Houthi-controlled Sanaa, the latest exchange in an escalation that has closed Riyadh's main airport and killed dozens this month. The Houthis have ordered civilians near Saudi oil facilities to evacuate, calling them legitimate targets, as Trump weighs joining the Saudi campaign.

top.headline: Airstrike on Disputed Sudan-Egypt Border Gold Mine Kills at Least 72
top.blurb: A Sudanese rights group says an airstrike killed at least 72 people, and by some survivor accounts far more, at a gold mine on the contested Sudan-Egypt border, the second deadly strike at the same site this year. The group blames the Egyptian air force, which has not commented; Sudan's army has ordered an investigation.

top.headline: Australia Rout South Africa by 214 Runs to Win First Durban Test
top.blurb: Josh Hazlewood took career-best figures of 6 for 49 to bowl out South Africa for 206 in their second innings, as Australia completed a 214-run win in the series opener at Kingsmead. Man-of-the-match Matthew Renshaw scored 272 runs across the match, in Australia's first meeting with South Africa since losing last year's World Test Championship final at Lord's.

top.headline: Chris Rock Returns to Directing With the High-Powered, If Problematic, 'Misty Green'
top.blurb: In his first film since 2014's 'Top Five,' Chris Rock directs and co-stars in 'Misty Green,' about a once-acclaimed actress, played by a 'fireball' Rosalind Eleazar, whose career has collapsed. NPR's Fresh Air critic John Powers calls it bursting with energy but says it heads toward bleaker territory than viewers might expect.

bengal.headline: Suvendu Adhikari Warns TMC Against Disrupting Durga Puja With Protests
bengal.blurb: West Bengal's BJP Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari warned Trinamool Congress against disrupting Durga Puja with protest rallies, as tension rises ahead of a TMC-backed march demanding the Election Commissioner's resignation.

travel.headline: 10 of the Best Neighborhoods in Athens
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet's guide to Athens ranks ten neighborhoods, from the Acropolis-adjacent Makrygianni and Koukaki to the nightlife of Psyrri and the quieter streets of Pangrati.

travel.headline: An Argentine Deep-Sea Canyon Yields 57 New Species, Despite the Hype Around 'Patrick'
travel.blurb: A two-week taxonomy workshop on specimens from Argentina's Mar del Plata Canyon identified 57 new marine species, including a horned sea cucumber nicknamed 'Loki' — though the viral 'Patrick' sea star wasn't among them.

happy.headline: The Mathematician Who Divided Genius Into the Ordinary and the Magicians
happy.blurb: In his memoir, probability theorist Mark Kac split scientific genius into the 'ordinary,' whose brilliant work you could in principle follow, and the 'magicians,' like Richard Feynman, whose insights stay inexplicable even once you understand the result.

tech_top.headline: Character.AI Files for Bankruptcy Just Five Years After Launch
tech_top.blurb: Character Technologies filed for Chapter 11 in Delaware, with Disney as lead 'stalking-horse' bidder at $20 million for a license to its chatbot technology, not the consumer app itself, which keeps running until a buyer is found or the business winds down by year's end. The filing caps a fast fall for a company Google paid roughly $2.7 billion to license technology from in 2024.
tech_top.pm_note: A well-funded, widely-used consumer AI product going bankrupt in five years is a reminder that engagement and burn rate don't equal a durable business — worth weighing on any build-vs-buy call for companion-AI features.

tech_top.headline: An AI Tool Lets Police Pinpoint a House From a Single Interior Photo
tech_top.blurb: Raven, from Graylark Technologies and formerly called GeoSpy, matches details like flooring, appliances and room layout in one photo against Airbnb, Vrbo and Zillow listings to identify the specific property it was taken in, without relying on metadata. The LAPD and Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office have both bought access; an earlier public version of the tool was shut down after 404 Media found it being used to track people.
tech_top.pm_note: Another surveillance-adjacent vendor selling directly to police departments with little disclosure of its technical pipeline — the same procurement-risk pattern as Flock, worth tracking if your own stack touches similar image-matching infrastructure.

tech_more.headline: Apple Launches a New $299 Apple TV 4K With Siri AI and Remote-Free Voice Commands
tech_more.blurb: Apple's refreshed Apple TV 4K adds an upgraded chip, Siri-powered content search and built-in microphones for remote-free voice commands, shipping November 13 for $299.

tech_101.text: An initial bid in a bankruptcy sale that sets the floor price and terms for a later auction — the role Disney's $20 million offer plays in Character.AI's Chapter 11 case, win or lose.

Identifying where a photo was taken by matching its visual details against known images, rather than reading GPS data embedded in the file — the technique behind tools like Raven that can place an interior photo at a specific address.

science.headline: Vanillin, the Flavor Compound, Shows Early Promise for Healing Wounds
science.blurb: Flinders University's Biomedical Nanoengineering Laboratory found that vanillin, the compound behind vanilla's flavor, has notable antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties in early lab testing. Researchers say the findings point toward vanillin-based wound-care dressings, though the work is still preclinical and has not been tested in patients.

science.headline: Webb Finds an Ancient Galaxy Cluster With Surprisingly Concentrated Dark Matter
science.blurb: Caltech-led analysis of a JWST-observed galaxy cluster more than 10 billion light-years away, XLSSC 122, found a dark matter concentration denser than cosmological models predict for a structure that old. It's the most distant cluster yet found acting as a strong gravitational lens, and lead author Kyle Finner says its mass doesn't fit standard predictions for how quickly the universe's biggest structures should form.

philosophy.headline: Why Real Intelligence Is Something More Than Optimisation
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Sasha Mudd grants that AI runs on optimisation — objectives, rewards and feedback loops that improve performance against a fixed standard — but argues optimisation can only say how to reach an end, never whether that end deserves pursuing. Drawing on Kant against Hume, she holds that genuine reason can question its own goals, which she thinks separates it from any machine.

philosophy.headline: The Velocity of War, and Why Faster Isn't Always Smarter
philosophy.blurb: Former British intelligence officer Andy Owen draws on Paul Virilio's concept of 'dromology' — the study of speed as a driver of war and politics — to argue that the race for ever-faster military and AI decision cycles is outrunning our ability to predict or control its risks. Deliberate slowness, he argues, is a strategic virtue rather than a weakness in an age built to reward speed.

philosophy_101.text: Paul Virilio's term for the study of speed as a driving force in politics and war — the lens Andy Owen uses to question whether faster decision-making is always the advantage it's assumed to be.
Reasoning that tells you how to get what you want but has nothing to say about whether you should want it — the limit Sasha Mudd argues optimization-based AI can't cross, however capable it gets.
